# Controlled Autonomy Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that agent autonomy is bounded, observable, interruptible, and evidence-backed
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Legend**: `[M]` mandatory (a constitution MUST, an approved requirement, or an approved decision); `[O]` optional enhancement or backlog boundary. `G0` is evaluable now against the approved specification, plan, ADRs, and contracts; `G1` is evaluable after `/speckit-tasks` and `/speckit-analyze`, before implementation. `{Detects: ...}` links an item to a failure pattern in the [README](README.md) detection matrix. Dimension tags: Completeness, Clarity, Consistency, Measurability, Coverage, Traceability, Edge Case, Assumption, Conflict, Gap.
## Bounded Scope

- [ ] CHK001 - Is each agent role's permitted-action scope enumerated, with an out-of-scope action defined as blocked and audited? [Completeness, Spec FR-109, Orchestration §9.3] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is it defined that agents never approve, grant exceptions, or hold the approver credential, with a failing case for each? [Coverage, Spec FR-109 NAC, DEC-037] [M, G0] {Detects: missing-approval-enforcement}
- [ ] CHK003 - Are all high-impact actions enumerated and mapped one-to-one to a gate? [Completeness, Constitution III, Plan §2.4] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are autonomy limits bounded in time and attempts (timeouts, retry cap, resumption cap) with safe-stop on exceeding them? [Measurability, Spec PVT-009, PA-002, PA-003] [M, G0] {Detects: unlimited-retries}
- [ ] CHK005 - Can an agent act past a mandatory policy FAIL? Is that defined as blocked? [Coverage, Spec FR-125] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK006 - Are agent read and write limits defined (filesystem, repository, path traversal, content addressing)? [Coverage, Security TH-10, TB-5] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK007 - Can the same agent author a test and be the sole reviewer, or modify tests to force a pass? Is that prohibited? [Coverage, Orchestration §9.3] [M, G0]

## Observability and Interruptibility

- [ ] CHK008 - Is every agent action audited with actor type and role, with the fields defined? [Completeness, Spec FR-130, Audit schema] [M, G0] {Detects: incomplete-audit-evidence}
- [ ] CHK009 - Is human interruption defined (cancel or stop at any state) with what remains afterwards? [Coverage, Control-plane contract, Spec FR-120] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the handling of hostile instructions embedded in requirement text defined, with an expected refusal outcome? [Edge Case, Security TH-06, Scenario C] [M, G0]

## Evidence Honesty and Review

- [ ] CHK011 - Are AI-generated artifacts defined as untrusted until human review, with the states complete, merge-eligible, and applied? [Clarity, Spec FR-133, DEC-001] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is autonomous deployment, finalization, or merge to a protected branch prohibited with a defined detection? [Coverage, Spec FR-133 NAC, Orchestration G-DESTR] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is HUMAN_AUTHORED_SUBMISSION fallback defined so it never lowers a gate or policy? [Coverage, Spec FR-118 NAC] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK014 - Are agent modes (LIVE_EXTERNAL, SCRIPTED, MIXED) defined with a rule that scripted output cannot be labelled live? [Measurability, ADR-005, POL-TRC-002] [M, G0] {Detects: fabricated-results}
- [ ] CHK015 - Must an agent's claim of a result (tests passed, scan clean) be backed by recorded evidence rather than assertion? [Coverage, Constitution X, Spec FR-129] [M, G0] {Detects: unsupported-completion-claims}
- [ ] CHK016 - Is the provider API agent adapter excluded and labelled backlog? [Coverage, Plan §6.1 BL-01] [O, G0]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Gap]` or `[Conflict]` name a place where the current documents are silent or disagree; they are findings for the reviewer to resolve, not pre-judged results
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially within this file (`CHK001` onward); cite them as `<file>:CHKnnn`
